annotation.venue: Report of the State Comptroller of Israel – Cyber and Information Systems
named_instruments_referenced: Israel National Program for Artificial Intelligence (2023)
annotation.summary_en: State Comptroller of Israel audit report (November 2024) on national AI preparedness. It finds Israel has no long-term national AI strategy, no integrating government body, slow and partial use of the Telem programme budgets, and falling international rankings. It recommends a comprehensive government-approved national AI plan with leadership, milestones and monitoring.
key_provisions_or_claims: Israel lacks a long-term national AI strategy and an integrating government body to oversee the national AI programme
Only 40% of the first-phase budget (NIS 220M of ~NIS 550M) was used; only 11% for supercomputing
Israel fell from 5th to 9th in the Tortoise index and from 20th to 30th in the Oxford government AI readiness index
Hebrew/Arabic LLM development was delayed; human capital funding served academia but not industry
Recommends that the Ministry of Innovation lead a full national programme with milestones and budget, monitored by the PM via the NSC
